bug_semantics: PQCipher.decrypt() in openssl_encrypt/modules/pqc.py hybrid-decrypts a Kyber KEM ciphertext with AES-256-GCM. When AESGCM.decrypt() raises (authentication/tag failure), the except path does not fail closed: it instead AES-CTR-decrypts the same ciphertext with the first 16 bytes of the derived key and nonce[:16] and returns that plaintext. There is no production/test guard, so any GCM failure — including an in-transit bit flip that invalidates the tag — is silently downgraded to unauthenticated, malleable CTR. An attacker who can modify ciphertext therefore bypasses integrity verification and can bit-flip recovered plaintext without detection. Affected public tags are v1.0.0 through v1.3.6 (< 1.4.0); 1.4.0+ refuse to decrypt on AEAD failure.
flaw_origin: The original PQC decrypt in c58b460ea6d9daaa0fd83fb8a924c71a8b8f9202 (still present at parent 295bf5f3df60ce08d2d8aed26d4fa0bc03592850) caught GCM failures and immediately raised ValueError('Decryption failed: authentication error') with no CTR path. 5e3104481d9842d3d6989332ae32bee4b010d2db first inserted the unauthenticated AES-CTR last-resort block into that except path (pqc.py ~694-790 at the BIC; ~1400-1444 at the pre-fix tree), labeled 'for testing only' but reachable whenever GCM failed. No finer public member exists: the commit is a single-parent first-write, modes.CTR is absent from the parent tree, and git log -L on the surviving comment traces only to this commit.
